messages:
Marta K: hey team — after last night's pager I think we should tighten our internal incident comms templates. a few asks: make tone more consistent, clarify placeholders so non-owners can fill them quickly, and add a short customer-facing snippet for status pages

Priya N: +1. also can we make the order of sections standard? TL;DR, impact, mitigation, ETA, next steps, contact. that helped on my last handoff.

Alex R: I ran into confusion about the 'customer impact' bit — some folks wrote long engineering details. propose: two separate blocks: "Customer-facing (2-3 lines)" and "Internal detail". the first must be copy-paste ready for status page/email.

Samir V: Agree. Suggest we include placeholders that are explicit, e.g., [INC-ID], [AFFECTED-REGION], [USER-IMPACT], [MIGRATION-STEP]. that stops ambiguous edits.

Jordan L: Drafted a compact template for customer-facing status updates — share for feedback: 
```
[TL;DR] Short one-line summary of impact.
[Impact] Which users/regions/features affected (2-3 bullets).
[Customer impact] What customers may observe, suggested workarounds.
[Mitigation in progress] What we're doing now and ETA for next update.
[Contact] Who to reach for questions (incidents@redwood.ai).
```

Mei Chen: Love the split. Tone note: be empathetic and avoid absolutes unless verified. e.g., "we may see" vs "we will". keep it confident but not overpromising. provide a short suggested phrasing bank for common scenarios.

Marta K: Good point Mei. Also: we should add a brief on-call handoff checklist to the template so the person taking over knows what to copy to status page, what to tell CS, and what logs to grab.

Samir V: Here's a proposed on-call checklist snippet to include in the internal section: 
```
- Current status (one sentence)
- Last action (who, when)
- Known mitigations & blockers
- Short list of next two actions (owner + ETA)
- Customer comms drafted? (Y/N) + link
```

incident-bot: Reminder: weekly incident-comms review scheduled in #eng-oncall on Mon @10am. See agenda: link to doc. :spiral_calendar:

Priya N: For wording library, propose we add a small table of canned lines for customers:
- "We are investigating reports of increased error rates affecting API requests in EU."
- "We have implemented a mitigation to reduce impact; customers may see transient timeouts."
- "No action required from customers at this time; we will update by [ETA]."

Alex R: Also add explicit instructions for status page updates frequency: initial within 15m of detection, follow-up every 30-60m until mitigation, final postmortem within 72h. we should make those the default SLA for comms.

Marta K: Decision proposal: adopt the standardized template + canned phrases + on-call checklist. docs team to own wording library updates. engineering to review on-call checklist and timing. volunteers?

Jordan L: I can help with the canned phrasing and examples for common incident types (latency, auth outages, degraded throughput).

Mei Chen: I'll own the doc updates and migration of the existing templates into the new format. will draft an editorial guide for tone (empathetic, concise, actionable).

Samir V: I'll update the incident runbook to include the new handoff checklist and add a short snippet on 'what to paste to a status page' so it's copy/paste ready.

Priya N: Quick nit: status page copy should avoid jargon. e.g., say "Customers may see delayed responses" vs "increased p99 latency" for customer-facing. keep metrics for internal only.

Marta K: Solid. Action items: Mei — draft new templates and tone guide (due in 3 business days). Samir — update runbook & checklist (due 4 business days). Jordan — canned phrase bank (2 business days). Alex & Priya — review SLAs for update cadence (2 business days). I'll schedule a 30m sync and ping docs for final merge.

incident-bot: Action created: "Comms template refresh" assigned to Mei Chen, due 3 business days.

Alex R: One more: include a short "what not to say" list (e.g., "we are still investigating" without context, or speculative root cause statements). helps juniors avoid problematic phrasing.

Marta K: Agreed. we'll add that to the editorial guide. thanks everyone — let's iterate and land this before next on-call rotation. :thumbsup:
